title: Federal League
capsule: The Federal League (Liga Federal) was a political and military alliance of the Banda Oriental's rural caudillo forces under José Gervasio Artigas, established in 1815 as a federalist alternative to Buenos Aires centralism after the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata declared independence. Artigas, styled Protector of the Free Peoples, drew together Entre Ríos, Corrientes, Santa Fe, Córdoba, and Misiones alongside the Banda Oriental in an attempt to create a loose confederation respecting provincial autonomy. The League disintegrated under simultaneous pressure from Porteño forces to the south and a Portuguese invasion of the Banda Oriental from 1816; by 1820 Artigas was forced into Paraguayan exile, ending the experiment.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The League's territorial claims are recorded in political documents but the effective territorial control of each member province fluctuated widely year to year; cartographic precision is low.
